l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.goal: Check whether di claim say di sum of two polynomials wey get x² terms also get x² term always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.material: Claim: When you add two polynomials wey get x² terms, di sum always still get x² term. Find di addition wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.s.s1.r.a: 3x² remain for di sum. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.s.s1.r.c: 2x² remain for di sum. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.s.s1.r.d: 4x² remain for di sum. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.s.s1.explain: x² and −x² add reach 0, so di sum 3x+2 no get x² term.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.s.s2.model.0: x²+(−x²)=0, so di sum become 3x+2, wey no get x² term, so e be counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-01.s.s2.model.1: Di x² terms of di two expressions get opposite signs, so dem disappear when dem add, wey make am counterexample.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.title: (a+b)² na di same as a²+b²?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.goal: Check whether di claim say (a+b)² always equal a²+b² always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.material: Claim: (a+b)²=a²+b² hold for any numbers a and b. Find a and b wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose di values of a and b wey go against di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s1.r.b: Both sides na 0, so dem equal. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s1.r.c: Both sides na 16, so dem equal. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s1.r.d: (0+6)²=36 and 0²+6²=36, so dem equal. Dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s1.explain: If a=2 and b=3, then (2+3)²=25 and 2²+3²=13, so dem differ.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s2.model.0: (2+3)²=25 but 2²+3²=13, so di two values differ. E be counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-02.s.s2.model.1: When one number na 0, di two sides equal by chance, but with 2 and 3 you go get 25 and 13, wey differ. So e be counterexample.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.goal: Check whether di claim say (x+1)² always big pass x²+1 always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.material: Claim: No matter which number you put for x, di value of (x+1)² big pass di value of x²+1. Find x wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s1.prompt: Choose di value of x wey go against di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s1.r.a: (4+1)²=25 big pass 4²+1=17, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s1.r.c: (1+1)²=4 big pass 1²+1=2, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s1.r.d: (2+1)²=9 big pass 2²+1=5, so dis example fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s1.explain: If x=−1, then (−1+1)²=0 and (−1)²+1=2, so 0 small pass.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s2.model.0: If you put x=−1, then (x+1)²=0 and x²+1=2, so di first value small pass. E be counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-10.s.s2.model.1: (x+1)²−(x²+1)=2x, so when x na negative di difference na negative. Na why x=−1 be counterexample.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.goal: Check whether di claim say di solutions of quadratic equation dey always be two different numbers dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.material: Claim: Quadratic equation dey always get two different solutions. Find one equation wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s1.prompt: Choose di equation wey go against di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s1.r.a: Di solutions na 1 and 5, two different numbers.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s1.r.b: Di solutions na −2 and 3, two different numbers.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s1.r.d: Di solutions na 2 and −2, two different numbers.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s1.explain: (x−3)²=0 give only x−3=0, so just one solution dey, x=3.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s2.model.0: (x−3)²=(x−3)(x−3), so only x=3 come out. Only one different solution dey, so na counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-17.s.s2.model.1: Di two factors dey di same, so only one x dey wey make am 0, wey be 3. Dis go against di claim say two solutions dey.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.material: Claim: If a<b, then a²<b² always too. Find a and b wey show say claim no correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.s.s1.prompt: Choose a and b wey go against di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.s.s1.r.a: 1<4, so a²<b² correct. Dis example support di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.s.s1.r.c: 4<25 correct. Dis example support di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.s.s1.r.d: 0<9 correct. Dis example support di claim.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.s.s2.model.0: −3<1, but (−3)²=9 bigger pass 1²=1, so a²<b² no hold. Na counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-25.s.s2.model.1: When you square negative number e turn positive and bigger, so inequality sign direction change for a=−3 and b=1.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.title: Product dey always big pass sum?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.goal: Check whether di claim "di product of numbers of cases dey always big pass di sum" dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.material: Claim: When two events get m ways and n ways, di product m×n dey always big pass di sum m+n. Find (m, n) wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.s.s1.prompt: Choose di (m, n) wey go against di claim.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.s.s1.r.b: Di product 36 big pass di sum 12, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.s.s1.r.d: Di product 12 big pass di sum 7, so dis one na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.s.s1.explain: If m=1 and n=3, di product na 3 and di sum na 4, so di product small pass.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.s.s2.model.0: 1×3=3 small pass 1+3=4, so di product no big pass di sum, wey make am counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-41.s.s2.model.1: To multiply by 1 no change number, so di product 3 become small pass di sum 4, and di claim break.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-01.s.s1.r.c: 125=125, so both sides equal. Dis na example wey fit di claim.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-02.s.s1.r.c: After dem simplify, 4 terms dey, so dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-02.s.s1.r.d: After dem simplify, 4 terms dey, so dis na example wey fit di claim.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.goal: Check whether di claim say di inequality sign dey stay di same when dem multiply both sides by di same number always true, find one case wey e no true (a counterexample), and explain am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.material: Claim: Even if you multiply both sides of an inequality by di same number, di direction of di inequality sign go stay di same. Multiply 3<5 by one number to show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s1.prompt: Which multiplier go against di claim?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s1.r.b: 1.5<2.5, so di direction stay di same. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s1.r.c: 30<50, so di direction stay di same. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s1.r.d: 12<20, so di direction stay di same. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s1.explain: If you multiply 3<5 by −2 e give −6 and −10, and −6>−10, so di direction change.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s2.model.0: To multiply by −2 give −6 and −10, and −6>−10, so di inequality sign flip, wey be counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-17.s.s2.model.1: To multiply by a negative number dey reverse di order of di numbers, so 3<5 become −6>−10.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.goal: Check whether di claim say di two roots of a quadratic equation always get di same sign always true, find one case wey e no true (a counterexample), and explain am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.material: Claim: Di two roots of a quadratic equation always get di same sign (both positive or both negative). Find one equation wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.s.s1.r.b: Di roots na 3 and 4, both positive. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.s.s1.r.c: Di roots na 2 and 3, both positive. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.s.s1.r.d: Di roots na −2 and −5, both negative. Dis na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.s.s1.explain: x²−x−6=(x−3)(x+2)=0, so di roots na 3 and −2, wey get different signs.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.s.s2.model.0: From (x−3)(x+2)=0 di roots na 3 and −2, so di signs differ, wey be counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-18.s.s2.model.1: If di constant term na negative, di product of di two roots na negative, so their signs differ. Na why dis equation break di claim.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.material: You roll one die. Claim: The number of outcomes for 'A or B' na always the number of outcomes for A plus the number of outcomes for B. Find one pair wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s1.prompt: Choose the 'A or B' wey go against the claim.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s1.r.a: {1,3,4,5} get 4 outcomes, wey equal the sum 3+1.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s1.r.c: {1,2,5,6} get 4 outcomes, wey equal the sum 2+2.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s1.r.d: {3,4,6} get 3 outcomes, wey equal the sum 2+1.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s1.explain: 3 even outcomes + 3 prime outcomes = 6, but 2 dey inside the two, so for real 5 dey.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s2.model.0: 2 na both even and prime, so dem count am two times when you add, wey give 5 outcomes, and na counterexample.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-32.s.s2.model.1: The face 2 overlap, so e be 5 outcomes, no be 3+3=6.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-01.material: Claim: If two points get different x-coordinates, the distance between dem always equal the difference of the x-coordinates (bigger value − smaller value). Find two points wey show say this claim wrong.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-01.s.s1.r.c: The distance na 7 and the difference of the x-coordinates na 7 too, so na example wey fit the claim.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.title: Add or Multiply: Wetin Decide Am?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.topic: Di Sum Rule and di Product Rule
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.goal: Decide which information (standard) you really need to know whether to add or multiply, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.material: 3 kinds of bread and 4 kinds of drinks dey. You want separate to choose "one of either bread or drink" from to choose "one bread and one drink."
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di standard to decide whether to add or multiply?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.o.a: Whether di two events happen together or only one happen
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.o.b: Whether di item names resemble each other
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.r.b: Di standard no be di names but whether you choose dem together.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.o.c: Whether di number of ways big or small
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.r.c: Di standard no be di size of di numbers but how di events happen.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.o.d: Whether di number of ways na even or odd
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.r.d: Even or odd no get anything to do with di way to calculate.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s1.explain: If you choose only one, na 3+4=7 ways, and if you choose one of each together, na 3×4=12 ways.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s2.model.0: Dem dey multiply events wey happen together, and dem dey add events wey only one of di two happen, so you need dis standard.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-35.s.s2.model.1: To be big number or even number no tell you how to calculate, so wetin matter na whether di events happen together.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.title: How we take know whether order matter?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.goal: Find out which criterion (information) you really need to decide whether to count with permutations or combinations, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.material: "To choose president and vice president from 5 people" and "to choose 2 cleaning duty people from 5 people" dem dey count am for different ways. By which criterion we take separate di two cases?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di criterion wey separate di two cases?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.o.a: Whether di names of di people wey dem choose dey di same
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.r.a: Di criterion no be di names but di roles or di order.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.o.b: Whether different order or role of those wey dem choose make different case
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.o.c: Whether di total number of people na even
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.r.c: Di total of 5 people dey di same for both cases.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.r.d: Both cases choose 2 people, so e no fit be di criterion.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s1.explain: President and vice president get different roles so order matter, while cleaning duty no get order.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s2.model.0: For president and vice president, if order change e be different case, so na permutation; cleaning duty na di same case, so na combination.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-43.s.s2.model.1: The two of dem dey choose 2 people, but dem differ for whether order dey change the result, so na that one be the criterion.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.title: Wetin we suppose look to add two matrices?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.goal: Work out which criterion (information) must dey to know whether dem fit calculate the two matrices A+B, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.material: Matrix A na 2×3 and B na 3×2. Something dey wey you must check first when you wan add the two matrices entry by entry.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the criterion to know whether dem fit add dem?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.o.a: Whether the diagonal entries dey the same
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.r.a: The diagonal entries no get anything to do with whether addition possible.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.o.b: Whether the number of rows and the number of columns dey the same for the two
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.o.c: Whether the sums of the entries dey the same
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.r.c: The sum of the entries no dey decide whether addition possible.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.o.d: Whether all the entries na positive
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.r.d: The signs of the entries no get anything to do with whether addition possible.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s1.explain: You dey add entries wey dey the same position, so the shapes must be the same. Dem no fit add 2×3 and 3×2.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s2.model.0: Entries wey dey the same position must pair up, so the number of rows and columns must match.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-50.s.s2.model.1: 2×3 matrix no get entries wey match those of 3×2 matrix, so whether the shapes dey the same na the criterion.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.title: Wetin must match to calculate di product AB?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.goal: Work out which criterion (information) dem must have to tell whether dem fit calculate di product AB, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.material: A na 2×3 matrix. You fit find di product AB with a 3×1 matrix B, but no with a 2×1 matrix. Explain di reason using di criterion.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di criterion for to fit calculate di product AB?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.o.a: Whether A and B get di same number of entries
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.r.a: Di number of entries no get anything to do with whether di product possible. 6 and 3 entries also work.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.o.b: Whether di number of columns of A and di number of rows of B na di same
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.o.c: Whether di number of rows of A and di number of rows of B na di same
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.r.c: For a product, dem pair di columns of A with di rows of B.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.o.d: Whether A and B get di same shape
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.r.d: Di shapes no need to be di same. 2×3 and 3×1 fit also multiply.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s1.explain: Di entries of AB come from to pair and multiply one row of A with one column of B, so di number of columns of A must equal di number of rows of B.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s2.model.0: Di number of entries for one row of A and for one column of B must equal to pair dem up and multiply, so di number of columns and di number of rows must equal.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-57.s.s2.model.1: 2×3 and 3×1 fit multiply because A 3 columns equal B 3 rows, but 2×1 no work because 3 and 2 differ.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.title: Wetin decide di degree of a polynomial?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.goal: Work out which criterion (information) dem must have to find di degree of di polynomial 3x²y+xy³−5, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.material: You want decide di degree of di polynomial 3x²y+xy³−5. Two variables dey, x and y, so you must decide which value to use as di criterion.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di criterion to decide di degree?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s1.r.a: xy³ get degree 4, di sum of di exponents of x and y. If you look only x, you go miss am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s1.r.b: Di coefficient 3 no get anything to do with di degree.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s1.o.c: Di largest among di values wey you get if you add all di exponents of di variables for each term
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s1.r.d: Even with three terms, di degree no be 3.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s1.explain: x²y get degree 2+1=3 and xy³ get degree 1+3=4. Di largest, 4, na di degree of dis polynomial.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s2.model.0: You add all di exponents of di variables for one term, so xy³ get degree 4, and di largest value, 4, na di degree.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-03.s.s2.model.1: If you look only x, you go miss di y³ for xy³, so di criterion na di largest among di values from to add all di exponents.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.title: Why x²−9y² fit factor but x²+9y² no fit?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.goal: Work out which criterion (information) dem must have to tell whether an expression factors as difference of two squares, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.material: x²−9y² factor into (x+3y)(x−3y). But x²+9y², wey resemble am, no fit factor with di same method. Find di criterion wey tell di two apart.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di criterion to tell whether e fit factor?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.o.a: Whether e dey di form of a difference (subtraction) of two squares
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.r.b: x²+9y² also get two terms, but e no fit factor.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.o.c: Whether all di coefficients na positive
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.r.c: Di criterion no be di sign of di coefficients but whether e dey subtraction form.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.o.d: Whether two kinds of variables dey
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.r.d: Even with two kinds of variables, a sum no fit factor.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s1.explain: A²−B²=(A+B)(A−B), so e must dey subtraction form. A²+B² no fit use dis formula.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s2.model.0: x²−9y² na di difference of x² and (3y)², so e fit factor reach (x+3y)(x−3y), but x²+9y² na sum, so you no fit use dis formula.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-04.s.s2.model.1: Di formula A²−B²=(A+B)(A−B) dey work for subtraction only, so di main thing wey you go check na whether na difference of two squares.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.title: Wetin be di difference between "at least" and "more than"?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.goal: Work out which standard (information) dem really need to tell x≥3 and x>3 apart, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.material: Both x≥3 and x>3 include numbers wey big pass 3. Still, di two inequalities differ. Find di standard wey tell dem apart.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di standard wey separate di two inequalities?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.o.b: Whether only multiples of 3 na solutions
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.r.b: Di solutions no limit to multiples of 3.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.o.c: Whether di solutions na only integers
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.r.c: Numbers wey no be integers na solutions of both inequalities.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.o.d: Whether numbers wey big pass 3 dey
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.r.d: Both inequalities include numbers wey big pass 3.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s1.explain: For x≥3, x=3 also na solution, but for x>3, x=3 no be solution.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s2.model.0: If you put x=3, x≥3 become true and x>3 become false, so whether 3 dey included na di standard.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-19.s.s2.model.1: Both get numbers wey big pass 3 as solutions, so dem differ only for whether 3 itself dey included.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.title: Wetin we need know make y=x²−4x+k meet di x-axis?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.goal: Work out which standard (information) dem really need to tell whether di graph of y=x²−4x+k meet di x-axis, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.material: y=x²−4x+k=(x−2)²+k−4. Di graph open upward. Which information we suppose consider to know whether e meet di x-axis?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.o.a: Whether di coefficient of x² na 1
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.r.a: Dem don know di coefficient 1 already and e no decide whether dem meet.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.o.b: Di position of di point where e meet di y-axis
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.r.b: Di point where e meet di y-axis no tell whether e meet di x-axis.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.o.c: Only whether di graph open upward
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.r.c: Di direction wey e open alone no tell whether e touch di x-axis.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.o.d: Whether di y-coordinate of di vertex na 0 or less
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s1.explain: E open upward, so if di y-coordinate of di vertex (2, k−4) na 0 or less, e meet di x-axis. Dat one mean k≤4.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s2.model.0: Di vertex na di lowest point, so e meet di x-axis when im height k−4 na 0 or less.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-20.s.s2.model.1: Even if e open upward, e no meet di x-axis when di vertex dey above di x-axis, so we must look di y-coordinate of di vertex.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-50.s.s1.o.b: Whether dem get di same numbers

l-m-h1-b0e01b-50.s.s1.r.d: Even if di sums equal, di entries fit different.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-50.s.s2.model.0: Di entries for di same positions different, so even with di same numbers, A and B no be di same matrix.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-50.s.s2.model.1: For matrix, position get meaning, so you judge am by whether di entries for every position equal.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.goal: To find di distance between two points, pick which criterion (piece of information) dem really need, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.material: You want find di distance between two points for a coordinate plane. Think about which information about di two points dem really need.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.prompt: Which information dem really need to find di distance?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.o.a: Both di x-coordinates and y-coordinates of di two points
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.o.b: Di slope of di line wey pass through di two points
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.r.b: Di slope alone no tell you how far apart di two points dey.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.o.c: Di quadrant wey di two points dey inside
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.r.c: Even inside di same quadrant, many points dey wey get different distances.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.o.d: Only di x-coordinates of di two points
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.r.d: If di y-coordinates differ, di distance go change too, so e no reach.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s1.explain: You need di difference of di x-coordinates and di difference of di y-coordinates of di two points to find di distance with di Pythagorean theorem.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s2.model.0: Dem find di distance from di difference of di x-coordinates and di difference of di y-coordinates, so dem need di coordinates of both points. Di slope or quadrant no tell you di distance.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-02.s.s2.model.1: To know only di x-coordinates no reach, because you no know how far apart di points dey for di y direction. Di distance dey fixed only when you know both coordinates.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-40.s.s1.o.a: The same y match different x

l-m-h1-b0e02a-40.s.s2.model.1: Function need one y for each input x, so if the same x get two or more y, e no be function.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-22.material: You wan find the complement of the set A={2,4,6}. Complement dey collect the elements wey no dey inside A, based on one bigger set. Think about wetin dem must get.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-22.s.s2.model.1: If you know only A and you no know U, you no fit talk which elements no dey inside A, so dem must get U.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-45.s.s2.model.1: If you draw 6 segments from each point e give 7×6=42, but dem count the same segment two times, so if you divide by 2 e give 21 segments.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-21.s.s1.r.c: Dis one just use di number for di right as e be.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-21.s.s2.model.1: Add 1 to both sides and then divide by 2, so from 2x<22 we go get x<11.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-35.s.s1.r.b: E no be 5×5. The tens place get 6 choices.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-35.s.s2.model.0: The tens place get 6 choices and the ones place get the remaining 5, so 6×5=30.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.title: As the sum dey get bigger, the number of cases go keep growing?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.goal: Find and talk one pattern inside several cases of the sum of the faces of two different dice and the number of cases, and check that pattern with one new case.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.material: When the sum of the faces na 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, the numbers of cases na 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 one by one. Think whether this pattern go keep going.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.s.s1.prompt: How many cases get sum of faces wey be 9?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.s.s1.r.a: The sum 7 get 6 cases, the most. After that e dey reduce.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.s.s1.r.c: This one assume say e dey keep growing by 1. After 7 e dey reduce.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.s.s1.explain: The sum 9 get 4 cases: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3). The sum 7 get the most, and after that e dey reduce.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.s.s2.model.0: If you count from (3,6) to (6,3) e give 4 cases, so the growing pattern no continue after the sum 7.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-36.s.s2.model.1: The face of each die na at most 6, so when the sum pass 7 the possible pairs dey reduce, wey give 4 cases.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-51.s.s1.r.a: Dem multiply 3 four times too, so 3⁴=81.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-51.s.s1.r.c: You no dey multiply di entries by 4; you dey multiply di matrix by itself four times.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-51.s.s1.r.d: Dem multiply 2 four times too, so 2⁴=16.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-51.s.s1.explain: Di diagonal entries na powers of 2 and powers of 3, and di rest na 0. D⁴=(16 0; 0 81).
l-m-h1-b0e01b-51.s.s2.model.0: Di diagonal entries 4, 8 and 9, 27 na powers of 2 and 3 one by one, so D⁴ get 16 and 81.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-51.s.s2.model.1: Di entries wey be 0 still remain 0, so you only need to calculate 2⁴=16 and 3⁴=81 for di diagonal.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.material: If you multiply M=(1 3; 4 5) by (2 0; 0 2), e give (2 6; 8 10), and if you multiply by (3 0; 0 3), e give (3 9; 12 15). Find the rule. (; mean say na next row)
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you go get if you multiply M by (5 0; 0 5)?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s1.r.b: Na the value from multiplying be this, no be from adding 5.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s1.r.c: The matrix wey you dey multiply by no dey come out the same way. The entries of M dey show for the result.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s1.r.d: No be only the diagonal 5 dey change; every entry become 5 times bigger.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s1.explain: To multiply by (a 0; 0 a) dey make every entry of M become a times bigger. If a=5, e go be (5 15; 20 25).
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s2.model.0: When a=2 and 3, every entry of M become 2 times and 3 times bigger, so when a=5 e go be 5 times bigger, and e go give (5 15; 20 25).
l-m-h1-b0e01b-52.s.s2.model.1: The rule be say every entry go become a times bigger, so work out 1·5, 3·5, 4·5, 5·5.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.topic: Distance from di origin to a point
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.goal: Find and talk one rule from several cases of di distance from di origin to a point, and check dat rule with a new case.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.material: Dem measure di distances from di origin O to each point: (3,4) na 5, (6,8) na 10, and (5,12) na 13. Use di same rule to predict di distance to (8,15).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s1.prompt: Which one na di right distance to (8, 15)?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s1.r.a: Dat one na x plus y. If you use am for (3,4) e give 7, wey no match di cases.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s1.r.c: Dat one na di value wey use only di larger coordinate. For (3,4) e na 5, no be 4.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na di average of x and y. For (3,4) e na 3.5, wey no match di cases.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s1.explain: Di distances na di square roots of 3²+4²=25, 6²+8²=100, and 5²+12²=169. 8²+15²=289 and 17²=289.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s2.model.0: Di distance na di square root of x²+y². 8²+15²=289 and 17×17=289, so di distance na 17.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-03.s.s2.model.1: For (3,4), di square root of 9+16=25 give 5, so by di same rule, 64+225=289, wey give 17.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.title: To find a rule from points on a line
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.goal: Find and talk one rule from several cases of di relationship between x and y for points on a line, and check dat rule with a new case.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.material: Di points on di line na (0,1), (1,3), (2,5), (3,7). Every time x increase by 1, y increase by constant amount. Wetin be y when x=10 on di same line?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di value of y when x=10?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s1.r.a: Dem read am as y increasing by 1 every time x increase by 1. For di cases, e increase by 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s1.r.c: Dem take am as y=2x, and leave out di value 1 for x=0.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s1.r.d: Dem read am as increasing by 3 every time. For di cases, e increase by 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s1.explain: y go up by 2 every time x go up by 1, and e na 1 when x=0. So y=2x+1, and when x=10, y na 21.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s2.model.0: y increase by 2 every time x increase by 1, and y na 1 for x=0, so y=2x+1. If you put x=10 e give 21.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-11.s.s2.model.1: If x go up 7 more from (3,7), y go up 2×7=14, so 7+14=21. Dis one sure because di rule constant.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.title: How to find di rule for di number of elements of union
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.goal: Find and talk one rule from plenty cases of di number of elements of union, then test di rule with new case.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.material: Dem write down di numbers of elements of two sets A and B. When n(A)=3 and n(B)=4, n(A∪B)=7 if n(A∩B)=0, 6 if e na 1, and 5 if e na 2. If n(A)=5, n(B)=6, and n(A∩B)=2, wetin be n(A∪B)?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di value of n(A∪B)?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.s.s1.r.b: You add only part of am, like 5+2. You need to subtract 2 from 5+6.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.s.s1.r.c: You add di overlapping 2. For di cases, di more dem overlap, di smaller e go be.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.s.s1.r.d: You add only 5+6 without to subtract di overlapping part 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.s.s1.explain: Dem count overlapping elements once only, so n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B)=5+6−2=9.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-22.s.s2.model.0: Every time di overlap grow by 1 element, di union shrink by 1, so e be n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B). 5+6−2=9.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.material: If n(A)=5 and n(A∩B)=2, then n(A−B)=3. If n(A)=7 and n(A∩B)=3, e be 4. If n(A)=6 and n(A∩B)=0, e be 6. If n(A)=9 and n(A∩B)=4, wetin be n(A−B)?

l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.s.s1.r.a: You add am, like 9+4. For the cases, e dey reduce by the number of elements wey overlap.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.s.s1.r.c: You use n(A∩B) just as e be. For the cases, 3, 4, and 6 different.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.s.s1.r.d: You ignore the overlap. If the overlap na 4, e go reduce.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.s.s1.explain: A−B na A wey dem comot the elements wey overlap with B, so n(A)−n(A∩B)=9−4=5.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.s.s2.model.0: Dem comot the elements wey overlap with B from A, so e be n(A)−n(A∩B). That one give 9−4=5.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-37.s.s2.model.1: 5−2=3, 7−3=4, and 6−0=6 all dey work, so if you use the same rule, e give 9−4=5.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-41.s.s1.r.b: That one na the value for x=5. For x=6, e go down by 3 again.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-43.material: When the taxi distance na 1, 2, 3, 4 km, the fare na 3000, 3500, 4000, 4500 won. For every 1 km wey add, the fare dey go up by the same amount. Wetin be the fare for 10 km?

l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.title: How to estimate di value of (x+2)(x−3) when x=0.1
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.goal: Estimate di value of (x+2)(x−3) when x na 0.1, decide di size or range wey fit, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.material: Estimate roughly how much (x+2)(x−3) be when x near 0.1, without to calculate am exactly. E go help if you treat x as 0.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s1.prompt: Which one dey closest to di value?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s1.r.b: Even when x near 0, (x+2) and (x−3) no be 0.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s1.r.c: (x−3) na negative, so di sign of di product na negative too.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s1.r.d: E be like say you add 2 and 3. You suppose multiply dem.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s1.explain: If x≈0, then (0+2)(0−3)=−6. Di real value 2.1×(−2.9)=−6.09 near −6 too.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s2.model.0: If you treat x as 0 e give 2×(−3)=−6, so around −6 correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-07.s.s2.model.1: Positive times negative na negative, and di size dey around 2×3, so e dey around −6.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.title: If one side grow by 1, how much di area of square go grow?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.goal: Estimate how much di area go increase when di side of square change from 20 to 21, decide di size or range wey fit, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.material: One square get side of 20 cm, and dem increase di side to 21 cm. Estimate how much di area grow by remembering (n+1)²=n²+2n+1.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s1.prompt: Around how much di area grow?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s1.r.b: When one side grow by 1, di area no dey grow by 1. Two strips dey form for di edges.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s1.r.c: Dat one count only one strip for di edge (20). Dem add two strips.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na di original area, 20². E no be di amount wey e increase.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s1.explain: (n+1)²−n²=2n+1, so for n=20 e be 41. Di area grow by around two edge strips (20+20), one for di width and one for di length.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s2.model.0: Di area become 441, wey be 41 more than di original 400, so around 40 cm² correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-08.s.s2.model.1: Dem add one strip of 20 for di width and one strip of 20 for di length, so e grow by around 40.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-37.material: The number of ways to line up 8 people na 8×7×6×5×4×3×2×1. Estimate am without you calculate am reach the end. 4 people get 24 ways and 6 people get 720 ways.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-37.s.s2.model.1: 6 people get 720 ways, and with two more people e become 56 times as many, so e be about tens of thousands of ways.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-04.s.s2.model.0: Di distance na √61, and since 7²=49 and 8²=64, 61 dey between dem. So di distance dey between 7 and 8.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-04.s.s2.model.1: 61 near 64, so √61 small pass 8 small, about 7.8. So e dey between 7 and 8.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.goal: Estimate di position of di point (6, 4) compare to di circle to decide di size or range wey fit, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.material: Di circle (x−3)²+(y+1)²=25 get center (3, −1) and radius 5. Di square of di distance between di point (6, 4) and di center na 3²+5²=34.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.prompt: Which one describe di position of di point (6, 4)?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.r.a: Di square of di distance na 34, no be 25, so e no dey on di circle.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.r.b: Di center na (3,−1). (6,4) na different point.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.o.c: Inside di circle (di distance small pass 5)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.r.c: 34 big pass 25, so e far pass di radius.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.o.d: Outside di circle (di distance big pass 5)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s1.explain: Distance²=34>25=5², so di point far from di center pass di radius, wey mean say e dey outside di circle.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-17.s.s2.model.0: Di square of di distance na 34 and di square of di radius na 25. 34 big pass, so di point dey outside di circle.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-30.material: Solution for di number of multiples of 2 or 5 from 1 to 20: Line 1: 10 multiples of 2 dey. Line 2: Di multiples of 5 na 5, 10, 15, 20, wey be 4. Line 3: 10+4=14.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-30.s.s2.model.1: For a union, dem count overlapping elements only once, so fix line 3 to 10+4−2=12.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.material: Solution for the linear function wey y na 5, 7, 9 when x na 1, 2, 3: Line 1: When x go up by 1, y go up by 2. Line 2: When x=0, y=5+2=7. Line 3: So y=2x+7.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.s.s1.r.b: When x dey small, y dey small too. For x=0, y small pass for x=1.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.s.s1.r.c: 5, 7, 9 dey go up by 2 each time. Dat one correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.s.s1.r.d: Na the result of using the 7 from the earlier line. The earlier line wrong first.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.s.s1.explain: x=0 small pass x=1, so y=5−2=3. The equation na y=2x+3.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.s.s2.model.0: x=0 na 1 less than x=1, so y also 2 less, 5−2=3, but dem calculate am as +2, so line 2 wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-47.s.s2.model.1: If you put x=1 inside y=2x+3, e give 5, so e correct. So fix line 2 to 3.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.title: To Change a Rectangle's Area to a Sum of Pieces
l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.goal: Change di area of a rectangle wey get width x+3 and height x+2 to another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.material: Dem divide a rectangle wey get width x+3 and height x+2 into four pieces wey get sizes x×x, x×2, 3×x, and 3×2.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.s.s1.prompt: Which expression show di area as di sum of di four pieces?

l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.s.s1.explain: Di four pieces na x², 2x, 3x, and 6. When you add dem together, dem make x²+5x+6.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.s.s2.model.0: Di area of di big rectangle na di sum of di four pieces, so e na x²+2x+3x+6, wey equal (x+3)(x+2) when you simplify am.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-07.s.s2.model.1: If you distribute (x+3)(x+2), you go get x·x, x·2, 3·x, and 3·2, so e equal di sum of di four pieces.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-12.material: You want change di polynomial x²+6x+9 to a product. When dem expand di new expression, e must become di original expression.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-12.s.s1.r.b: When you expand am, e become x²−9.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-12.s.s2.model.1: Di constant term 9 na 3², and di coefficient of x, 6, na twice 3, so e equal (x+3)².

l-m-h1-b0e01a-22.material: x²−x−6=(x−3)(x+2), so di solutions of di equation x²−x−6=0 na 3 and −2. Talk dis solutions with di graph of di quadratic function y=x²−x−6.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-46.material: For the tree diagram, the 3 kinds of T-shirts na the first branches, and 2 kinds of trousers connect to each T-shirt. The number of end branches na the number of ways to choose.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-46.s.s1.r.b: You multiply the number of T-shirts two times, no be the trousers.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-46.s.s1.r.d: 3 kinds of T-shirts dey. No be 2 kinds.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-46.s.s2.model.1: The same shape repeat 3 times, so if you add 2 3 times e give 6, and as multiplication expression e be 3×2.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.title: How you go describe a midpoint as a movement?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.goal: Rewrite di midpoint M of segment AB for another form (expression, table, picture, words) and explain why e get di same meaning.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.material: Di point exactly for di middle of di path from A(2, 5) to B(6, 9) na M(4, 7). Talk M again with words wey describe am as a "movement".
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.prompt: Which one na di right way to talk M(4, 7) again?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.o.a: Di halfway point from di origin to B
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.r.a: Dem take di starting point wrongly as di origin instead of A.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.o.b: Di point wey you get if you add di coordinates of A and B
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.r.b: To add give (8, 14). For a midpoint, you add and then divide by 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.o.c: Di point wey you reach if you go 4 to di right and 4 up from A
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.r.c: Dat point na B. A midpoint go only half of di way.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.o.d: Di point wey you reach if you go 2 to di right and 2 up from A
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s1.explain: B−A=(4,4), and to go half of dat, (2,2), from A give (4,7).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s2.model.0: From A to B you go 4 across and 4 up, so di middle na di point wey you reach if you go 2 across and 2 up. Dat give (4,7).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-06.s.s2.model.1: Di middle of di x-coordinates 2 and 6 na 4, and di middle of di y-coordinates 5 and 9 na 7, so e na di same point.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.title: How to talk y = 2x − 4 with words
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.goal: Change di linear function y=2x−4 to another form (equation, table, picture, words) and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.material: We wan describe di linear function y=2x−4 with words instead of equation. Think about wetin di slope and di y-intercept mean.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.prompt: Which description mean di same thing as di equation?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.o.a: When x go up by 1, y go up by 2, and when x=0, y na −4
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.o.b: When x go up by 1, y go down by 4, and when x=0, y na 2
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.r.b: You swap di places of di slope and di y-intercept.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.o.c: When x go up by 1, y go up by 2, and when x=0, y na 4
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.r.c: You miss di sign of di y-intercept.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.o.d: When x go up by 2, y go up by 1, and when x=0, y na −4
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.r.d: You read di slope 2 upside down as 1/2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s1.explain: Di slope 2 mean say y go up by 2 when x go up by 1, and di y-intercept −4 na di value of y when x=0.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s2.model.0: Di slope 2 mean say y go up by 2 when x go up by 1, and di y-intercept −4 na y when x=0, so dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-14.s.s2.model.1: If you put x=0 e give y=−4, and if you put x=1 e give y=−2. E go up by 2, so di description with words match di equation.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.topic: Basics of di equation of circle
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.title: How to talk di equation of circle with words about distance
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.goal: Change di circle (x−1)²+(y−2)²=9 to another form (equation, table, picture, words) and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.material: We wan describe di circle (x−1)²+(y−2)²=9 as collection of points instead of equation. Read am to see wetin di center and radius be.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.o.a: Di collection of points wey dey distance 3 from di point (−1, −2)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.r.a: You read di sign of di center di opposite way. Di center na (1,2).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.o.b: Di collection of points wey dey distance 9 from di point (1, 2)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.r.b: 9 na di square of di radius. Di radius na 3.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.o.c: Di collection of points wey dey distance 3 from di point (1, 2)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.o.d: Di collection of points wey dey distance 3 from di point (2, 1)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.r.d: You swap di places of x and y. Di center na (1,2).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s1.explain: (x−1)²+(y−2)² na di square of di distance between (x,y) and (1,2), and 9=3², so di distance na 3.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s2.model.0: (x−1)²+(y−2)² na di square of di distance to (1,2), so if im value na 9, di distance na 3. Na why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-19.s.s2.model.1: If you put di point (4,2), wey dey 3 to di right of (1,2), e give 9+0=9, so point wey dey distance 3 satisfy di equation.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.title: Put A∩B inside words
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.goal: Change di symbol A∩B to another form (equation, table, picture, words) and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.material: Two sets dey: A={1,2,3,4} and B={3,4,5}. A∩B={3,4}. Try explain di symbol A∩B with words.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.prompt: Which statement mean di same thing as A∩B?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.o.a: Di group of elements wey dey inside A and B both
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.o.b: Elements wey dey inside A but no dey inside B
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.r.b: Dat one na di difference set A−B.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.o.c: Elements wey no dey inside A
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.r.c: Dat one na di complement of A.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.o.d: Elements wey dey inside at least one of A or B
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.r.d: Dat one na di union A∪B.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s1.explain: A∩B dey collect only di elements wey dey common to both sets, so e be {3,4}.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s2.model.0: A∩B dey collect only di elements wey dey inside both sets, so e be {3,4}. Na why e be di group of elements wey dey inside both.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-25.s.s2.model.1: 3 and 4 dey inside A and B both, so dem dey inside di intersection, but 1 and 5 dey inside only one of dem, so dem no enter.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.title: Put proposition inside di language of Venn diagram
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.goal: Change "If a number is a multiple of 4, it is a multiple of 2" to another form (equation, table, picture, words) and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.material: We wan show di proposition "If a number is a multiple of 4, it is a multiple of 2" with Venn diagram. Make P be di group of multiples of 4 and Q di group of multiples of 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.prompt: Which description of picture mean di same thing as dis proposition?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.o.a: Circle Q dey completely inside circle P
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.r.a: 6, wey be multiple of 2, no be multiple of 4, so Q no dey inside P.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.o.b: Di two circles dey exactly di same
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.r.b: 6 dey inside Q but e no dey inside P, so dem different.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.o.c: Circle P dey completely inside circle Q
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.o.d: Di two circles no overlap at all
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.r.d: 4 dey inside both, so one overlapping part dey.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s1.explain: All multiples of 4 na multiples of 2, so all di elements of P dey inside Q. So circle P dey inside circle Q.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s2.model.0: All multiples of 4 na multiples of 2, so every element of P dey enter Q. So circle P dey inside circle Q.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-33.s.s2.model.1: 6 dey inside Q but e no dey inside P, so di picture wey P dey inside Q na di correct one, no be di one wey Q dey inside P.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.title: To read quadratic function graph with words
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.goal: Turn the graph of the quadratic function y=−x²+4 into another form (equation, table, picture, words), then explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.material: You wan describe the graph of the quadratic function y=−x²+4 with words, without picture. Think about wetin the sign of the coefficient −1 of x² and the 4 mean.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.o.a: E open downward and the vertex na (0, 4)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.o.b: E open downward and the vertex na (0, −4)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.r.b: Because of the +4, the y of the vertex na 4.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.o.c: E open upward and the vertex na (0, 4)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.r.c: If the coefficient of x² negative, the graph go open downward.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.o.d: E open downward and the vertex na (4, 0)
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.r.d: The 4 na y-value. When x=0, y=4.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s1.explain: The coefficient of x² na −1, so e open downward, and the maximum value na 4 when x=0, so the vertex na (0,4).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s2.model.0: The coefficient negative, so e open downward. When x=0, y=4, and for other x e dey reduce, so the vertex na (0,4).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-44.s.s2.model.1: −x² na 0 or less, so y no fit pass 4, wey mean say the top na (0,4).

l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.title: To turn a description of a graph into a linear function equation
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.goal: Turn a description into a linear function equation, wey be another form (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.material: One line go down 3 for y every time x go up 1, and y na 5 when x=0. Turn dis description into an equation of di form y=ax+b.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.s.s1.prompt: Which equation mean di same thing?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.s.s1.r.a: y dey decrease, so di slope na negative.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.s.s1.r.c: y na 5 when x=0, so di y-intercept na +5.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.s.s1.explain: If y decrease by 3, di slope na −3, and if e na 5 when x=0, di y-intercept na 5, so y=−3x+5.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.s.s2.model.0: Di slope na −3 and di y-intercept na 5, so y=−3x+5. If you put x=1 e give 2, wey small pass by 3, so e correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-52.s.s2.model.1: E na 5 for x=0 and e decrease by 3 every time x go up 1, so for x=2 e na 5−6=−1. If you put am inside di equation e also give −1, so dem match.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.title: Wetin go be good way to calculate 103×97?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.goal: Compare two methods or claims for how to calculate 103×97, choose di one wey better, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.material: Dem calculate 103×97 for two ways. A: multiply am directly with long multiplication. B: calculate (100+3)(100−3)=100²−3²=9991.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s1.o.a: B use di sum-and-difference formula and calculate only easy numbers
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s1.o.b: B wrong because e suppose add 3²
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s1.r.c: 103×97=9991, so di answers of both methods na di same.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s1.o.d: Only A correct. Dem dey use formulas only for letters
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s1.r.d: You fit use multiplication formulas with numbers too.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s1.explain: Both methods give 9991. B calculate only easy numbers like 100 and 3, so e simple pass.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-08.s.s2.model.1: Both methods give 9991, but B use only numbers wey easy to calculate for your head, so e fit better.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.goal: Compare two methods or claims for how to calculate (3x²+2x)−(x²−4x), choose di one wey fit pass, and explain wetin make you think so.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.material: A: 3x²+2x−x²−4x=2x²−2x. B: 3x²+2x−x²+4x=2x²+6x. Dem remove di parentheses for different ways.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.s.s1.o.b: A. Only di sign of di first term need change

l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.s.s1.r.c: Signs get rules, so only one answer dey.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.s.s1.o.d: B. Di − for front of di parentheses change di signs of all di terms inside
l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.s.s2.model.0: For −(x²−4x), di sign of −4x change to +4x too, so B correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-16.s.s2.model.1: A wrong because e leave di sign of −4x as e be, so B, wey change di signs of all terms, correct.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.title: Two ways to solve x²=4
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.goal: Compare two methods or claims for solving x²=4, choose the one wey fit pass and explain your reason.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.material: A: x²−4=(x+2)(x−2)=0, so x=2 or x=−2. B: x²=4, so x=2. Di two answers different.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.o.a: B. Na only 2 get square wey equal 4.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.o.b: A. (−2)² too na 4, so two solutions dey, −2 and 2.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.o.c: Both correct. You fit choose any solution wey you like.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.r.c: You need find all di solutions of equation.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.o.d: B. You no fit square negative number.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.r.d: You fit square negative numbers too, and (−2)²=4.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-23.s.s1.explain: (−2)²=4, so x=−2 too na solution. Two solutions dey, 2 and −2.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.title: To choose 2 representatives from 4 people: na 6 ways or 12 ways?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.goal: Compare two methods or claims for how to choose 2 representatives from 4 people, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain wetin make you think so.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.material: Choose 2 representatives from 4 people, without caring about order. X: 4×3=12 ways. Y: 4×3÷2=6 ways. A·B and B·A na di same pair of representatives.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s1.r.a: To choose happen together, so no add; think about to multiply.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s1.o.b: X. 4×3 itself na di number of ways to choose representatives.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s1.r.b: Dat value count A·B and B·A as different cases.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s1.r.c: Dem count each pair 2 times because of order, so you divide by 2.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s1.o.d: Y. Dem count di same two people twice each, so you divide by 2.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s1.explain: A·B and B·A na di same, so if you divide 12 ways by 2 e give 6 ways.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s2.model.0: Dem count di same pair of two people 2 times because of order, so 12÷2=6 ways correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-39.s.s2.model.1: Order no matter for representatives, so Y, wey divide 4×3=12 by 2, correct.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.title: Make we list the combinations or make we multiply?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.goal: Compare two methods or claims to count combinations of 20 kinds of menu items and 15 kinds of drinks, choose the one wey suit pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.material: With 4 kinds of menu items and 3 kinds of drinks, we fit list dem one by one and count 12 ways. If 20 kinds of menu items and 15 kinds of drinks dey, which method suit pass?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.o.a: Listing. Multiplying only work for small numbers.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.r.a: The multiplication principle dey work the same way even when the numbers big.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.o.b: Multiplying. 20×15=300 count everything without missing any.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.o.c: The answers differ, so we no fit use any of dem.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.r.c: Listing and multiplying give the same answer.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.o.d: Listing. Listing dey always more accurate.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.r.d: If you list plenty things, e easy to miss some or repeat some.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s1.explain: By the multiplication principle, e be 20×15=300 ways. Listing go take long time and e easy to get am wrong.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s2.model.0: You fit find 20×15=300 sharp-sharp, so multiplying faster and more accurate than to list 300 ways.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-47.s.s2.model.1: The more cases dey, the easier e be to miss some, so to use the multiplication principle suit pass.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.title: We fit talk say AB and BA equal?
l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.goal: Compare two methods or claims about the matrices AB and BA, choose the one wey suit pass, and explain your reasoning.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.material: When A=(1 2; 0 1) and B=(1 0; 1 1), AB=(3 2; 1 1) and BA=(1 2; 1 3). X: AB and BA always equal. Y: For general, dem different.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.s.s1.prompt: Which one of the two claims suit, and why?

l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.s.s1.r.a: The product of matrices fit change if you swap the order.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.s.s1.o.b: Y. For this example AB and BA different, so dem no always equal.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.s.s1.r.c: AB and BA get different entries, as the values above show.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.s.s1.o.d: The two correct. E depend on the case.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-54.s.s2.model.1: Even one counterexample mean say you no fit talk say dem always equal, so Y correct.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-13.goal: Compare two ways or claims for how to expand (x+2)(x+3), choose di one wey fit pass, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-13.material: A: I use di distributive law write x·x+x·3+2·x+2·3 and simplify am. B: I use di formula (x+a)(x+b)=x²+(a+b)x+ab straight. Both of us get x²+5x+6.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-13.s.s1.o.d: Na only di formula correct and di distributive law wrong
l-m-h1-b0e01b-13.s.s1.r.d: Di distributive law na basic method wey you fit use for any product.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-13.s.s1.explain: You fit always use di distributive law, and di formula na quick way when di form fit.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-13.s.s2.model.1: Di distributive law dey work for every product, so use dis method when di form different.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.title: Two solutions wey count two-digit numbers wey get 0
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di two-digit numbers wey dem make with cards 0, 1, 2, 3, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain why.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.material: Use two of di cards 0, 1, 2, 3 to make different two-digit numbers. A: 4×3=12 numbers. B: 3 choices for di tens place and 3 choices for di ones place, so 3×3=9 numbers.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.o.a: Dem both correct. Na only say dem count am different way
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.r.a: Di answers different, 12 and 9, so dem no fit both correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.o.b: A. 0 fit dey di tens place too
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.o.c: B. 0 no fit dey di tens place
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.o.d: A. 0 no fit dey di ones place
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.r.d: 0 fit dey di ones place, like for 10.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s1.explain: Di tens place get 3 choices: 1, 2, 3, and di ones place get di 3 cards wey remain (including 0). So 3×3=9 numbers.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s2.model.0: 01, 02, 03 no be two-digit numbers, so B, wey count 3 choices for di tens place, correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-42.s.s2.model.1: Di tens place no fit be 0, so B, wey count 3×3=9, na di one wey fit.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.title: How many ways exactly 2 heads fit show?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di ways 2 heads fit show among 3 different coins, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain why.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.material: Toss 3 different coins and count di ways exactly 2 heads go show. A: (H, H, T) na 1 way. B: 3 ways, based on which coin show tails.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.r.a: Na only 3 ways dey to get 2 heads.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.o.b: A. Na only head-head-tail get 2 heads
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.r.b: (H, T, H) and (T, H, H) get 2 heads too.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.o.c: A. Dem no separate di coins
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.r.c: If di coins different, you fit know which coin show tails.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.o.d: B. E depend on which coin show tails
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s1.explain: You just decide which of di 3 coins go show tails, so 3 ways dey.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s2.model.0: (H, H, T), (H, T, H), (T, H, H) all get 2 heads, so 3 ways dey and B correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-43.s.s2.model.1: To choose di coin wey go show tails get 3 possibilities, so 3 ways dey.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.title: A+B and B+A equal?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.goal: Compare two methods or claims about how to swap the order for matrix addition, choose the one wey better, then explain the reason.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.material: A=(1 2), B=(3 4). P: For matrix addition, the result go be the same even if you swap the order. Q: Order dey matter for matrices, just like for multiplication, so A+B and B+A different.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s1.o.a: P. Dem the same because na to add numbers entry by entry
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s1.r.b: A+B and B+A always dey the same.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s1.o.c: Q. Order dey matter for all matrices
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s1.r.c: Addition dey give the same result even if you swap the order. E no be like multiplication.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s1.r.d: B+A na (4 6) too. The positions of the entries no dey change.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s1.explain: A+B=(4 6) and B+A=(3+1 4+2)=(4 6), so dem the same, because you dey add the numbers for the same positions.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s2.model.0: (1+3 2+4) and (3+1 4+2) both na (4 6), so dem the same even if you swap the order.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-60.s.s2.model.1: You dey add the numbers for the same positions, and addition of numbers dey the same even if you swap the order, so P correct.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.title: If dem fit work out AB, dem fit work out BA too?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.goal: Compare two methods or claims about whether dem fit work out the products AB and BA, choose the one wey better, then explain the reason.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.material: A na 2×3 matrix and B na 3×1 matrix. P: If dem fit work out AB, dem fit always work out BA too. Q: Even if dem fit work out AB, dem fit no work out BA.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.o.a: P. Order no get anything to do with whether you fit multiply
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.r.a: For matrices, e depend on the order, the product fit work or e fit no work.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.o.b: Q. For BA, B 1 column and A 2 rows no match
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.o.c: Both wrong. Dem no fit work out AB too
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.r.c: Dem fit work out AB because A 3 columns and B 3 rows equal.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.o.d: P. The results of the two products get the same shape
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.r.d: AB na 2×1, and dem no even fit work out BA.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s1.explain: Dem fit work out AB as 2×1 because 3 columns and 3 rows match, but dem no fit work out BA because B 1 column and A 2 rows no match.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s2.model.0: For BA, B number of columns, 1, and A number of rows, 2, different, so dem no fit work am out, and Q correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-61.s.s2.model.1: Even if AB fit work, if you swap the order, the pairs no go match, so dem no fit work out BA.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.title: To compare two solutions wey find di midpoint
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di midpoint of di origin and (6, 8), choose di one wey better, and explain di reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.material: Find di midpoint of A(0, 0) and B(6, 8). Student P: di average of di coordinates, (3, 4). Student Q: di distance na 10, so half na 5, so (5, 5).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s1.r.a: Di two results na different points, so both no fit correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s1.o.b: P: You suppose average di coordinates, no be di distance
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s1.r.c: (3,4) na point wey dey 5 away from each of A and B.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s1.o.d: Q: Na half di distance, so na di midpoint
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s1.r.d: Dem use di distance 5 like coordinate. (5,5) dey √50 away from A.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s1.explain: (3,4) dey 5 away from both A and B. (5,5) dey √50 from A, so e no be di midpoint.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s2.model.0: (3,4) dey 5 from both A and B, so e dey exactly for di middle. (5,5) dey √50 from A, so e no be di midpoint.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-07.s.s2.model.1: For a midpoint you average di x's and di y's separately, so P correct. Di distance 5 na length, no be coordinate.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.title: Two lines wey get di same slope and different intercepts
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.goal: Compare two ways or claims about whether y=2x+1 and y=2x−3 meet, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.material: Two students dey talk about whether di two lines y=2x+1 and y=2x−3 meet. Student A: Di slopes na di same and di intercepts different, so dem parallel. Student B: If di intercepts different, dem go meet somewhere.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.prompt: Whose statement correct, and wetin be di reason?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.o.a: B: If di intercepts different, dem go meet for di end
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.r.a: Dem go meet when di slopes different. If di slopes na di same, di gap go remain di same.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.o.b: A: For di same x, y always differ by 4, so dem no go meet
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.r.c: "Dem meet" and "dem no meet" no fit both correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.o.d: B: If di slopes na di same, dem always be di same line
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.r.d: If di intercepts different, dem be different lines.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s1.explain: For di same x, di difference between di two y values na (2x+1)−(2x−3)=4, always di same. So dem no go meet.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s2.model.0: Di difference between di y values for di same x always na 4, so di two lines no go meet. A correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-15.s.s2.model.1: If you solve 2x+1=2x−3 e give 1=−3, wey no get solution, so dem no go meet. If di slopes na di same, di lines parallel.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.topic: Basics of di equation of circle
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.title: How to compare equations of circle wey get center (2,−3) and radius 4
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.goal: Compare two ways or claims about di equation of circle wey get center (2,−3) and radius 4, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.material: Two students write di equation of di circle wey get center (2, −3) and radius 4. Student A: (x−2)²+(y+3)²=4. Student B: (x−2)²+(y+3)²=16.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.o.a: Di center part wrong, so dem both wrong
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.r.a: Dem write di center (2,−3) correct as (x−2) and (y+3).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.o.b: Di two equations na di same circle
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.r.b: Di right sides different, 4 and 16, so dem be different circles.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.o.c: B: Di right side na di square of di radius, 4²=16
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.o.d: A: Write di radius 4 as e be for di right side
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.r.d: Di right side get di square of di radius, no be di radius.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s1.explain: Di right side of circle equation na r². Since r=4, e be 16, and di center (2,−3) dem write am as (x−2) and (y+3).
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s2.model.0: For circle equation di right side na r², and since r=4 e be 16. A get 4, so dat one na circle wey get radius 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-18.s.s2.model.1: (x−2)²+(y+3)²=16 give center (2,−3) and radius 4, so B correct.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.title: Two ways to read di difference set A−B
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.goal: Compare two ways or claims about di difference set A−B, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.material: A={1,2,3,4}, B={3,4,5}. Student X: A−B na di elements of A wey no dey inside B, so e be {1,2}. Student Y: A−B na wetin remain after dem join A and B together and comot di overlap, {1,2,5}.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.o.a: Y: If you comot di overlap, e go be {1,2,5}, and dat one correct
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.r.a: 5 no be element of A, so e no fit dey inside A−B.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.o.b: A−B and B−A always dey di same
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.r.b: B−A={5}, and dat one different from A−B={1,2}.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.o.c: X: Comot only di elements of A wey overlap with B
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.o.d: Di results of di two solutions dey di same
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s1.explain: A−B na only di elements of A wey no dey inside B, so e be {1,2}. 5 no dey inside A, so e no go enter.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s2.model.0: A−B na {1,2}, wey be A after dem comot di 3 and 4 wey overlap with B. 5 no be element of A, so e no go enter.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-26.s.s2.model.1: Di difference set na di elements wey dey inside A but no dey inside B, so e be {1,2}. Di 5 for Y answer no dey inside A.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.title: Two ways to check "Every prime number is odd"
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.goal: Compare two ways or claims about "Every prime number is odd," choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.material: Two students dey check di proposition "Every prime number is odd." Student A: 3, 5, 7, 11 all na odd, so e true. Student B: 2 na prime but e be even, so e false.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.o.a: A: Odd primes plenty pass, so e true
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.r.a: Even if dem plenty, e false if one wey no fit dey, wey be 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.o.b: A: Di more examples, di more sure say e true
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.r.b: No matter how many examples you collect, you never check every case.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.o.c: B: One counterexample dey make am sure say e false
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.r.d: 2 na prime number wey im only divisors na 1 and 2.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s1.explain: One counterexample don do to show say proposition false. 2 na prime and even both, so the proposition false.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s2.model.0: 2 na prime and even both, so one counterexample dey make am sure say the proposition false. B sure pass.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-34.s.s2.model.1: A check only few examples, so e no guarantee every case. With the counterexample 2, e false.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.goal: Compare two methods or claims for the minimum of y=x²−2x−3, choose the one wey better, then explain the reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.material: Table for y=x²−2x−3: when x na −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, y na 0, −3, −4, −3, 0. Student A: The smallest value for the table, −4, na the minimum. Student B: When x=0, y=−3 na the minimum.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.o.a: A: The smallest value na the maximum
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.r.a: The smallest value na the minimum.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.o.b: B: The y-intercept for x=0 na the minimum
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.r.b: When x=1, e na −4, wey small pass −3.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.o.c: The two solutions give the same value
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.o.d: A: For the table, −4 small pass −3
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s1.explain: For the table, when x=1, y=−4, wey small pass −3 for x=0. The graph open upward, so the lowest point na the minimum.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s2.model.0: If you put x=1, e give 1−2−3=−4, wey small pass −3 for x=0, so −3 no be the minimum. A correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-45.s.s2.model.1: For graph wey open upward, the lowest point na the minimum, so the smallest value for the table, −4, na the minimum.

l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di cost of 100 minutes on two plans, choose di one wey better, and explain di reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.material: Plan A get basic fee of 2000 won plus 100 won per 1 minute, and Plan B no get basic fee and charge 150 won per 1 minute. Which one cheaper for 100 minutes of use?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s1.prompt: Which plan cheaper for 100 minutes, and why?
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s1.o.a: B: E no get basic fee, so e cheaper
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s1.r.a: Even with no basic fee, di per-minute fee high pass, so e reach 15000 won.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s1.o.c: A: E get basic fee, so e always cost pass
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s1.r.c: Di per-minute fee small pass, so if you use plenty, A cheaper.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s1.o.d: A: E na 12000 won, cheaper than B own 15000 won
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s2.model.0: A na 2000+100×100=12000 won and B na 150×100=15000 won, so A cheaper by 3000 won.
l-m-h1-b0e02a-53.s.s2.model.1: Di per-minute fee differ by 50 won, so di more you use, di better A be, wey mean say A cheaper for 100 minutes.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.title: Compare di distance along di road and di direct distance
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di straight-line distance between two points and di distance along di road, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.material: Dem dey go from A(1, 1) to B(7, 9). Student C: waka 6 across and 8 up and talk say e be 14. Student D: talk say di distance wey join di two points directly na di square root of 6²+8²=100, wey be 10.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.prompt: Who find di distance between di two points, and why?
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.o.a: C: Di length wey dem waka, 14, na di distance
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.r.a: 14 na di length wey dem waka along across and up, and di straight-line distance na 10.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.o.b: D: 10 na di average of di horizontal and vertical
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.r.b: Di average of di horizontal and vertical na 7. 10 na di square root of di sum of squares.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.r.c: If dem find di same distance, di values suppose be di same, but dem be 14 and 10.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.o.d: D: Di straight-line distance wey join dem directly na 10
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s1.explain: Di distance between two points na di straight-line distance, so √(6²+8²)=10. 14 na di length wey dem waka along di road.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s2.model.0: Di distance between two points na di length of di straight line wey join dem directly, so e be 10. C own 14 na di length wey dem take go di long way.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-13.s.s2.model.1: 6²+8²=100 and 10×10=100, so di straight-line distance na 10.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.title: Compare two ways to find di x-intercept
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di x-intercept of di line y=−2x+6, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.material: Two students find di x-intercept of di line y=−2x+6. Student A: Put y=0 to get 0=−2x+6, x=3. Student B: Put x=0 to get y=6, so di x-intercept na 6.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.o.a: A: Di x-intercept na di x when y=0
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.o.b: B: Di value when x=0 na di x-intercept
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.r.b: Di y-value 6 when x=0 na di y-intercept.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.r.c: The x-intercept na only one, so 3 and 6 no fit both correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.o.d: A: This one na solution wey find the y-intercept
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.r.d: E put y=0, so e find the x-intercept.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s1.explain: The x-intercept na the point wey touch the x-axis, so y=0. From −2x+6=0, x=3.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s2.model.0: Point for the x-axis get y=0, so A, wey put y=0, correct. x=3.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-14.s.s2.model.1: The 6 wey B find na the y-intercept, so e no be the x-intercept. The x-intercept na (3,0).

l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.topic: Basics of di equation of circle
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.title: To compare two students wey read the center of one circle
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.goal: Compare two methods or claims for the center of the circle (x−5)²+(y+2)²=9, choose the one wey better, then explain the reason.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.material: Two students read the center of the circle (x−5)²+(y+2)²=9. Student A: The center na (5, −2). Student B: The equation show −5 and +2, so the center na (−5, 2).
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.o.a: A: The coordinates of the center na (−5, 2)
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.r.a: If you put (−5,2), the brackets no go turn 0.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.o.b: The two solutions na the same point
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.o.c: B: You fit just read the signs for the equation as dem be
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.r.c: (x−5) na 0 when x=5, so you must read the signs the opposite way.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.o.d: A: If you put x=5, y=−2, the brackets go turn 0
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s1.explain: If x=5 then x−5=0, and if y=−2 then y+2=0, so the point wey both squares turn 0 na the center.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s2.model.0: The center na the point wey both brackets turn 0, so A, wey put x=5, y=−2, correct with (5,−2).
l-m-h1-b0e02b-15.s.s2.model.1: If you put (−5,2), you go get (−10)²+4=104, so e no be the center.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.title: To compare two ways of how to count di elements of a union
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.goal: Compare two methods or claims for di number of elements for di union of A={1,2,3,4} and B={3,4,5}, choose di better one, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.material: Two students find di number of elements for di union of A={1,2,3,4} and B={3,4,5}. Student P: Count 3 and 4 only once, wey give {1,2,3,4,5}, wey be 5 elements. Student Q: 4+3=7 elements.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.o.a: Q: For 4+3, di overlapping numbers get added extra
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.r.a: You must subtract di overlapping numbers, no add dem.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.o.b: P: Di overlapping 3 and 4 suppose count only once
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.o.c: Both solutions give di same value
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.o.d: Q: Just add di counts of di two sets
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.r.d: 3 and 4 dey count twice. Dem suppose count only once each.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s1.explain: For a union, dem count overlapping elements only once. 4+3−2=5, so P correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s2.model.0: 3 and 4 dey both A and B, but for di union dem count dem only once, so e na 4+3−2=5 elements.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-33.s.s2.model.1: Q count di two overlapping elements twice, so e get 7, wey wrong.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.title: Two ways to examine "If x²=4, then x=2"
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.goal: Compare two methods or claims about "If x²=4, then x=2," choose di better one, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.material: Two students examine di proposition "If x²=4, then x=2." Student P: When x=2, e give 4, so e true. Student Q: x=−2 squared also na 4, and −2 no be 2, so e false.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s1.o.a: Q: x=−2 na counterexample where di hypothesis hold but di conclusion wrong
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s1.o.c: P: E work when x=2, so e true
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s1.r.c: One example wey fit no reach to call am true.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s1.o.d: P: 2 na di only number wey im square na 4
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s1.r.d: (−2)²=4, so 2 no be di only one.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s1.explain: x=−2 satisfy x²=4, but e no be x=2. Counterexample dey, so di proposition false.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s2.model.0: (−2)²=4, so e satisfy di hypothesis, but −2 no be 2, so e na counterexample. Q correct.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-34.s.s2.model.1: P check only x=2, so P miss −2. If even one counterexample dey, e false.

l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.title: Compare two water tanks wey dey leak
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.goal: Compare two methods or claims about di amount of water wey remain after 20 minutes, choose di one wey fit pass, and explain your reasons.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.material: Tank A get 100 L and e dey lose 5 L for every 1 minute. Tank B get 60 L and e dey lose 2 L for every 1 minute. After 20 minutes, which tank get more water remain?
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.prompt: Which tank get more water after 20 minutes, and why?
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.o.a: B: 20 L remain, wey pass A own 0 L
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.o.b: A: e start with more, so more go remain
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.r.b: A dey reduce fast, so after 20 minutes e get 100−5×20=0 L.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.o.c: Both tanks get di same amount remain
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.r.c: A get 0 L and B get 20 L, so dem different.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.o.d: A: e start with 100 L and e lose only 20 L for 20 minutes
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.r.d: Di amount wey e lose for 20 minutes na 5×20=100 L.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s1.explain: A: 100−5×20=0 L, B: 60−2×20=20 L, so B get more remain.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s2.model.0: A na 100−5×20=0 L and B na 60−2×20=20 L, so B get 20 L more.
l-m-h1-b0e02b-53.s.s2.model.1: A dey reduce plenty faster, so even though e start with more, B get more remain after 20 minutes.

l-m-h1-b0e01a-55.material: Di first week table get 2 stores as rows and Mon, Tue, Wed as columns (2×3). Di second week table get Mon, Tue, Wed as rows and 2 stores as columns (3×2). Keep di ledger format (rows = stores).

l-m-h1-b0e01a-55.s.s1.r.d: Di ledger format of rows = stores go break.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-55.s.s1.explain: Dem must get di same shape to add, and di same cell must be di same store and day.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-55.s.s2.model.0: If you rearrange di second week table to rows = stores, e go become 2×3 like di first one, so dem fit add and di ledger format go dey kept. Na why dis method correct.
l-m-h1-b0e01a-55.s.s2.model.1: If you just move cells, di stores and days go mismatch, so you must rearrange am while you keep di meaning.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.title: Conditions for how to design expression wey fit factor
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.goal: For quadratic x²+bx+c wey fit factor, weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other, choose di compromise wey fit pass, and explain why.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.material: Make x²+bx+c factor as (x+p)(x+q). Conditions: p and q na different natural numbers, b na at most 8, and c suppose big as e fit.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.s.s1.prompt: Which expression fit pass for di conditions?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.s.s1.r.a: E be (x+4)², so p and q na di same, wey break di conditions.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.s.s1.r.d: E follow di conditions, but c=12 small pass 15.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.s.s1.explain: (x+3)(x+5)=x²+8x+15 get p≠q, b≤8, and c=15, wey be as big as e fit be.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.s.s2.model.0: If p=3 and q=5, then b=8 and c=15, and p≠q, so e follow di conditions and c na di biggest.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-16.s.s2.model.1: 4 and 4, where p and q na di same, dem no allow am, and among different numbers wey get sum of at most 8, 3 and 5 get di biggest product, so dem correct.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-29.s.s2.model.1: 16 apples weigh 5.3 kg, wey pass, so the biggest number wey follow the conditions na 15.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.title: How to choose quadratic equation wey e roots fit the conditions
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.goal: For quadratic equation wey e two roots fit the conditions, weigh all the conditions wey conflict, choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.material: Choose quadratic equation x²−bx+c=0. Conditions: the two roots na different positive integers, the constant term c na at most 20, and the sum of the two roots big as e fit (among the choices).
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s1.prompt: Which equation suit pass for the conditions?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s1.r.a: The roots na 5 and 5, so dem no be two different roots.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s1.r.b: The constant term na 28, wey pass 20.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s1.r.d: E follow the conditions, but the sum of the roots na 8, wey small pass 9.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s1.explain: x²−9x+20=(x−4)(x−5) get roots 4 and 5, c=20, and the sum na 9.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s2.model.0: The roots na 4 and 5, different positive integers, with c=20 and sum 9, so e follow the conditions and e get the biggest sum.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-31.s.s2.model.1: x²−11x+28 get c=28, wey pass 20, and x²−10x+25 get double root, so x²−9x+20 correct.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-44.material: Set = one main + one side + one drink. Preparation cost (for 10,000 won): 3 for each main type, 2 for each side type, 1 for each drink type. Conditions: at least 30 set combinations, cost at most 20 (200,000 won), and among dem, di lowest cost.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.title: Conditions for how to decide di presentation order
l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.goal: Weigh all di conditions wey dey fight each other for di presentation order of A, B, C, D, choose di best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.material: Four teams A, B, C, D go present once each, one after di other. Conditions: A first, D come after B, C no be last, and if e possible C come before B.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.s.s1.prompt: Which order fit di conditions pass?
l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.s.s1.r.a: D dey before B and C dey last, so e break di conditions.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.s.s1.r.d: E meet di conditions, but e no meet di wish say C go come before B.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.s.s2.model.0: For A, C, B, D, A first, D come after B, and C no be last, so di conditions wey dem must meet don meet, and C dey before B too.
l-m-h1-b0e01b-46.s.s2.model.1: A, B, C, D meet di conditions wey dem must meet too but e no meet di wish, so A, C, B, D fit pass.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-47.material: A bus routes dey from house go di transfer station and b subway routes dey from di transfer station go school (number of ways a×b). Conditions: at least 10 ways, di route total a+b suppose small as e fit, and if dem tie, di one wey get more ways.

l-m-h1-b0e01b-47.s.s1.r.b: Di route total na di same, 7, but e get 10 ways, wey small pass di 12 ways of (3,4).
